## Synthesis Overview

PR #259 is a minimal documentation update to `docs/features/opencode-runtime.md`, adding a sentence acknowledging that the auditor family carries the same developer-local Tavily and Context7 MCP dependencies as the researcher family. All three reviewers independently identified the same primary defect: the newly added sentence omits `auditor.md` itself from the explicit file list, even though `auditor.md` has both `io.github.upstash/context7/*` and `io.github.tavily-ai/tavily-mcp/*` enabled in its frontmatter (verified at lines 33–34 of `.opencode/agents/auditor.md`). The degree of model agreement on this core finding is very high. Claude additionally identified that `AGENTS.md` — the canonical onboarding entry point loaded by `opencode.json` — was not updated and still names only the researcher family as carrying these dependencies.

**Model Agreement Score:** 8/10 — near-unanimous on the primary finding; one unique finding from Claude; one severity divergence between Gemini and the other two.

Claude noted the implicit cause of the omission — the "independent" qualifier — and verified that `synthesizing-auditor.md` is correctly excluded (no Tavily/Context7 in its frontmatter). **GPT** identified the same primary finding with a concise, well-supported description and confirmed the base auditor's frontmatter manually. **Gemini** also found the primary finding but rated it Critical rather than Warning, and did not investigate companion files or the `synthesizing-auditor.md` exclusion.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

```
[U-W-01] `auditor.md` omitted from the explicit MCP dependency file list
Severity: Warning (2/3 models; see Divergence Analysis [D-01])
Category: Documentation / Correctness
File: docs/features/opencode-runtime.md
Lines: ~197 (the newly added paragraph)
Detail: The updated paragraph reads: "...plus the independent auditor sub-agents
`auditor-kimi.md`, `auditor-qwen.md`, and `auditor-glm.md`, rely on Tavily and Context7..."
The parent `auditor.md` agent carries the same two MCP tool enablements
(`io.github.upstash/context7/*: true` and `io.github.tavily-ai/tavily-mcp/*: true`) at
lines 33–34 of its frontmatter, confirmed by direct inspection. Only `synthesizing-auditor.md`
is correctly excluded (it carries no Tavily/Context7 entries). The parallel researcher-family
sentence lists all five researcher files including the parent `researcher.md`; consistency and
accuracy both require `auditor.md` to appear alongside the three sub-agents.
A developer reading this page to configure their local Opencode environment would conclude
that only the three model-specific auditor variants need Tavily/Context7 configured, leaving
`auditor.md` non-functional at runtime without a clear diagnostic.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Replace "plus the independent auditor sub-agents `auditor-kimi.md`,
`auditor-qwen.md`, and `auditor-glm.md`" with "plus `auditor.md`, `auditor-kimi.md`,
`auditor-qwen.md`, and `auditor-glm.md`". The word "independent" can be dropped — it was the
implicit framing that caused the exclusion of the parent file.
```

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

```
[S-W-01] `AGENTS.md` companion file not updated — researcher family only
Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: AGENTS.md
Lines: ~30
Detail: AGENTS.md line 30 reads: "The researcher family depends on developer-local Tavily and
Context7 MCP servers configured in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; the checked-in
`opencode.json` keeps only project-level runtime settings plus Chroma." This sentence was
not updated in the PR and now contradicts the corrected statement in
`docs/features/opencode-runtime.md`. Verified by reading the current file on disk — the
sentence is unchanged and names only the researcher family. AGENTS.md is the file loaded by
`opencode.json`'s `instructions:` field and is the canonical onboarding entry point; a
developer starting there receives an incomplete picture even after the PR lands.
Model: Claude only
Assessment: Genuine finding. Claude verified the file is not updated (confirmed by direct
inspection during synthesis). The fix is a straightforward one-line prose extension — "The
researcher and auditor families depend on..." — and is directly analogous to the main PR fix.
GPT and Gemini likely did not check companion files; neither stated the file was correct,
so this is absence-of-check rather than disagreement. The companion-file sweep rule in the
shared review process explicitly targets exactly this situation.
Suggestion: Update AGENTS.md ~line 30 to: "The researcher and auditor families depend on
developer-local Tavily and Context7 MCP servers configured in
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; the checked-in `opencode.json` keeps only project-level
runtime settings plus Chroma."
```

## Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Severity of [U-W-01]: Warning vs Critical
Claude says:  Warning — documentation omission, one-line prose fix, zero code risk
GPT says:     Warning — incomplete documentation, fixable prose update
Gemini says:  Critical — factually incorrect documentation about which agents require setup

Assessment: Claude and GPT are more calibrated here. The affected file is documentation,
not production code. The practical impact is runtime confusion when invoking `auditor.md`
directly without Tavily/Context7 configured, but this is a missing-doc scenario rather than
a bug or security issue. The distinction between "Critical" and "Warning" in this project's
review rubric maps better to code defects (Critical) vs documentation gaps (Warning).
Gemini's "Critical" framing reflects genuine concern about developer-facing impact but
overstates the severity tier for a pure documentation PR.
Resolution: Classify as Warning. Address before merge — but it is a low-risk one-line fix.
```
